dedupe_keys.name: opentreemap urban tree inventory and ecosystem services platform

description: OpenTreeMap is an open source web platform for crowdsourced urban tree inventories that also estimates the ecosystem services of each tree, used by cities and community groups to manage street trees and engage residents. It covers any municipality or region that deploys it: users can search and add trees, edit records with species, location, height, plot and condition, load existing tree datasets, export tree lists as KML or CSV, and calculate greenhouse gas, water, energy and air quality benefits from species and diameter; deployments have included PhillyTreeMap and the San Diego Tree Map. It was developed by Azavea with support acknowledged from the USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture. The otm-core code is available from GitHub under the GNU Affero General Public License, free of charge, with separate iOS and Android apps; the former hosted subscription site at opentreemap.org showed unrelated content when read today, so the hosted service appears discontinued. Caveats: the code depends on external keys for Google Maps and Rollbar and is no longer offered as a service. It remains useful as a template for community tree inventories that feed stormwater, heat and green infrastructure assessments; a related record is the i-Tree model suite.
